subject: Targeted peering partition in EU/APAC — recovery options & customer opt-in for traffic fallback
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme-corp.com, lucy.wong@acme-corp.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, alex.martinez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T03:12:00Z
Subject: Targeted peering partition in EU/APAC — initial notice and immediate mitigation options

Good morning Lucy / Acme Ops team,

Quick note to let you know we detected a targeted peering partition affecting parts of our EU and APAC egress zones starting ~03:00 UTC. Impact: a subset of requests originating in EU and APAC regions to hosted inference nodes experienced elevated connection timeouts and retries, which raised tail latency for some customers.

What we did immediately:
- Activated emergency routing rules to steer affected traffic to alternate peering within the same region where available.
- Enabled temporary cross-region failover to neighbouring EU pools for non-data-residency workloads.
- Deployed a KV-prefix cache warmup for long-lived sessions to reduce token pressure during reroute.

Customer-facing options (what you can choose):
1) Stay on current routing: we will continue to trial intra-region reroutes; you may see intermittent 5xx or elevated latency for some requests until peering is healthy.
2) Opt-in to automatic cross-region fallback: we can flip a controlled policy to send traffic to our EU->US or APAC->US pools (best for availability; may affect latency and data residency).
3) Configure client retries to tolerate transient errors (we can provide a small client-side patch).

Ask: please reply with your preferred option. If you want us to opt you in to automatic fallback, reply with: "OPT-IN FALLBACK" + preferred target region (us or eu). If we do not hear back in 6 hours we will keep current routing and continue targeted mitigations.

I'll follow up with a concise post-incident note and draft postmortem once we stabilize.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Attachment(s): None in this message
From: Lucy Wong <lucy.wong@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-10-04T04:03:22Z
Subject: Re: Targeted peering partition in EU/APAC — initial notice and immediate mitigation options

Karthik — thanks for the heads up.

Short answers:
- Our workload for the next 12 hours is latency-sensitive; cross-region could add jitter.
- Data residency: we need EU-only for persisted logs, but inference traffic can be routed to non-EU short-term as long as logs remain EU-bound.

Can you confirm whether opting-in will keep logs (and any personal data) routed to our EU storage? Also please provide an ETA on when you expect peering to be fully restored.

— Lucy
Lucy Wong
Platform Reliability Lead, Acme Corp
ops@acme-corp.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.com, alex.martinez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T08:15:00Z
Subject: RE: Targeted peering partition in EU/APAC — internal status and recommended fallback plan

Karthik / team — quick internal status update and recommendation before we reply to Lucy: 

Root cause: EuroCloud reported an asymmetric peering table update on two IX links (AMS and FRA) that caused a subset of session handshakes to drop for flows with large initial window sizes. EuroCloud says they will have a patch out in ~3–4 hours, but that depends on their maintenance window.

Impact characterization: ~7% of EU traffic and ~5% APAC egress affected for customers with large streaming sessions. Most short-lived requests are unaffected.

Recommended customer-facing fallback (preferred safe default):
- Offer controlled fallback to US pools for inference compute only, with logs and telemetry still routed to EU storage endpoints. We have a sidecar patch that splits control plane routing (EU only) and inference plane (fallback). Latency delta for Acme should be ~30–80ms median.
- Prepare an SDK toggle and a one-line feature flag in the dashboard that the customer can flip back when peering is confirmed healthy.

I'll prep the postmortem draft and an opt-in template (YAML) for customers to sign if they require explicit approval.

Vanessa
Director, Customer Reliability Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme-corp.com, lucy.wong@acme-corp.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, alex.martinez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T12:07:45Z
Subject: Post-incident note & opt-in instruction — peering partition, draft postmortem attached

Lucy / Acme Ops,

Thanks for the quick reply and the constraints — noted on data residency for logs. Per Vanessa's assessment we can implement a safe fallback that routes inference compute to our US pools while preserving logs and persisted telemetry to your EU storage endpoints. This keeps you available while maintaining EU residency for stored data.

Attached: postmortem-draft-20261004.pdf (short timeline + remediation) and traffic-fallback-opt-in-template.yaml (one-line YAML you can paste into your config or send back signed).

What opting in does (concise):
- Routes inference compute to US fallback pool(s) for your live requests until we confirm peering recovery.
- Leaves control plane, logs, and storage endpoints pointed at EU locations.
- Applies a temporary client-side retry policy we recommend enabling (we provide a 2-line SDK patch).

If you want us to proceed, reply with a single line: "OPT-IN FALLBACK -> us". If you prefer to wait, reply "HOLD" and we will leave current routing in place and continue mitigations.

We will also share a final postmortem within 48 hours once EuroCloud confirms the fix and we validate traffic health.

Best,
Karthik
Attachment(s): postmortem-draft-20261004.pdf (6 pages), traffic-fallback-opt-in-template.yaml
From: ops@acme-corp.com <ops@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: lucy.wong@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-10-04T18:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-incident note & opt-in instruction — peering partition, draft postmortem attached

Karthik — Acme opts in.

OPT-IN FALLBACK -> us

Please proceed with the fallback and confirm when traffic has shifted. We will apply the SDK retry patch during the maintenance window at 19:00 UTC. Also please confirm that persisted logs remain in EU storage during the fallback.

Thanks,
Acme Ops Team
